destinations.name: Lisbon
destinations.tagline: Mild winter sun and hilltop views.

details.why: The summer crowds are gone and the days are still mild. On 11 November the city celebrates São Martinho, and roasted chestnut carts fill the street corners.

go.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
go.map: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte, Lisbon
go.note: One of the highest viewpoints in the city. Arrive half an hour before sunset.

go.name: Alfama before 10am
go.note: Wander the old lanes before the tour groups arrive.

go.name: Belém
go.note: Jerónimos Monastery, then custard tarts at Pastéis de Belém.

go.name: LX Factory
go.note: A former industrial complex full of shops, bars and the Ler Devagar bookshop.

skip.name: Tram 28 at midday
skip.note: Packed, slow and a favourite with pickpockets.
skip.instead: Ride it before 9am, or walk the route.

skip.name: The Santa Justa Lift queue
skip.note: A long wait for a very short ride.
skip.instead: Walk to the top from Largo do Carmo.

skip.name: Restaurants with touts on Rua Augusta
skip.instead: Eat at a local tasca in Graça or Campo de Ourique.

dishes.name: Bacalhau à Brás
dishes.note: Shredded salt cod scrambled with straw potatoes, egg and onion. The dish to start with.

dishes.name: Amêijoas à Bulhão Pato
dishes.note: Clams cooked with garlic, olive oil, lemon and coriander. Mop up the sauce with bread.

dishes.name: Peixinhos da horta
dishes.note: Green beans in a light batter, fried until crisp. The name means "little fish from the garden".

dishes.name: Pastel de nata
dishes.note: Flaky pastry filled with caramelised custard, best eaten warm with cinnamon.

places.name: Ramiro
places.note: A busy seafood hall on Avenida Almirante Reis, known for its clams. Expect a queue at peak times.

places.name: Laurentina, O Rei do Bacalhau
places.map: Laurentina O Rei do Bacalhau, Lisbon
places.note: A long-standing restaurant on Avenida Conde Valbom devoted to salt cod.

places.name: Manteigaria
places.note: Custard tarts baked in front of you, with several branches across the city.

history.name: The Age of Discoveries
history.note: Vasco da Gama sailed for India from Belém in 1497. The riches of the spice trade paid for the Jerónimos Monastery, begun a few years later.

history.name: The 1755 earthquake
history.note: On 1 November 1755 an earthquake, a tsunami and days of fire destroyed most of the city. The straight streets of the Baixa are the rebuild that followed.

history.name: Alfama
history.note: The oldest quarter, with a street plan that goes back to Moorish times. It came through 1755 better than the lower town, which is why its lanes still twist.

history.name: 25 April 1974
history.note: The Carnation Revolution ended almost half a century of dictatorship, nearly without bloodshed. The red suspension bridge over the Tagus is named after the date.

nightlife.name: Bairro Alto
nightlife.note: Hilly lanes packed with small bars, cheap drinks and crowds that spill into the street. The liveliest area after dark.

nightlife.name: Pink Street, Cais do Sodré
nightlife.note: A former red-light street turned bar strip. Pensão Amor is the best-known stop, and MusicBox has live music and DJs.

nightlife.name: Fado at Tasca do Chico
nightlife.note: A small, informal fado bar with two branches. Bairro Alto is livelier, Alfama more intimate. Go early, it fills fast.

nightlife.name: Lux Frágil
nightlife.note: The city's best-known club, in a former warehouse by the river with a rooftop bar. The door is selective, so dress the part.

destinations.name: Kotor
destinations.tagline: A dramatic bay, quiet lanes and off-season prices.
destinations.go: The Ladder of Kotor at dawn
destinations.skip: The Old Town on cruise ship days

details.why: The summer crowds have gone and prices drop, but the bay is at its most dramatic. Pack a raincoat: November is one of Kotor's wettest months, so save the climbs for a dry morning.

go.name: The Ladder of Kotor at dawn
go.note: A free switchback trail above town with sweeping views of the bay. Start early and wear proper shoes.

go.name: Perast
go.note: A tiny baroque town about 20 minutes along the bay, facing the island church of Our Lady of the Rocks.

go.name: A konoba in the Old Town
go.note: Warm up in a traditional tavern with Njeguši ham, local cheese and a glass of Vranac red.

go.name: The Old Town after 5pm
go.note: Once the day-trippers leave, the squares, churches and famous cats have the place back.

skip.name: The Old Town on cruise ship days
skip.note: Day-trippers can pack the narrow lanes from late morning.
skip.instead: Check the port's cruise schedule and explore early or after 5pm.

skip.name: The €15 fortress climb on a wet day
skip.note: The limestone steps get slippery and the view can vanish into cloud.
skip.instead: Wait for a dry morning. From 1 December the climb is free.

skip.name: Driving into the Old Town area
skip.note: Parking is scarce and expensive, and clamping is common.
skip.instead: Park outside the centre and walk in.

dishes.name: Mussels na buzaru
dishes.note: Boka Bay mussels cooked in white wine, garlic, olive oil and parsley.

dishes.name: Crni rižot
dishes.note: Black risotto coloured with cuttlefish ink, a legacy of Venetian rule.

dishes.name: Njeguški pršut and cheese
dishes.note: Smoky dry-cured ham and sheep's cheese from the mountain village of Njeguši, above the bay.

dishes.name: Ispod sača
dishes.note: Lamb or veal slow-roasted under an iron dome covered in embers. Hearty, and right for a wet November day.

places.name: Konoba Scala Santa
places.note: A family-run konoba on Trg od Salate in the Old Town, known for black risotto and fish stew.

places.name: Stari Mlini
places.note: A restaurant in a centuries-old mill by the water at Ljuta, along the bay. Fish, mussels and a clay-pot dish of the day.

places.name: Marenda Grill House
places.note: Grilled meat a short walk outside the Old Town walls. Check opening hours before you go, as winter schedules vary.

history.name: A walled port
history.note: Kotor has been a trading port since Roman times. St Tryphon's Cathedral, at the heart of the Old Town, was consecrated in 1166.

history.name: Venice, 1420 to 1797
history.note: Almost four centuries of Venetian rule gave the town its walls, palaces and the winged lions still carved above its gates.

history.name: The 1979 earthquake
history.note: A major earthquake badly damaged the Old Town in April 1979. The same year UNESCO listed Kotor as a World Heritage Site, and the restoration took years.

nightlife.name: November is quiet
nightlife.note: Kotor's nightlife is a summer affair. Off season, evenings mean a long dinner and a drink in the Old Town rather than clubs, and some bars close for a few weeks.

nightlife.name: Old Winery Wine Bar
nightlife.note: Local Vranac by the glass with a plate of ham and cheese, and jazz in the background.

nightlife.name: Pub Old Town
nightlife.note: A lively pub with an international crowd, open all year.

nightlife.name: Maximus
nightlife.note: The big club built into the walls by the Sea Gate. It peaks in July and August, and in winter it opens only for events, so check first.

details.why: On 27 November Ljubljana switches on its festive lights and its December celebrations begin. Come earlier in the month for quiet streets and lower prices, or late for the lights. Mornings are often foggy, so save the views for the afternoon.

go.name: Prešeren Square, 27 November
go.note: The festive lights switch on at 5pm, opening the city's December celebrations.

go.name: The Central Market
go.note: Fresh produce, cheese and local snacks by the river. Go in the morning, Monday to Saturday.

go.name: Ljubljana Castle
go.note: Walk up for views over the red rooftops. Best in the afternoon, once the morning fog lifts.

go.name: Metelkova
go.note: Former army barracks turned into a graffiti-covered alternative arts quarter.

skip.name: The castle funicular
skip.note: You pay for a ride that lasts about a minute.
skip.instead: Walk up from the old town in around 15 minutes.

skip.name: Driving into the centre
skip.note: The old town is largely car-free and parking is expensive.
skip.instead: Use a park-and-ride on the edge of the city and take the bus in.

skip.name: Lake Bled as a rushed half day
skip.note: November days are short, and a quick trip means more time on the bus than at the lake.
skip.instead: Give it a full day, or save it for another trip.

dishes.name: Štruklji
dishes.note: Rolled dough dumplings with fillings such as cottage cheese, walnut or apple, served sweet or savoury.

dishes.name: Kranjska klobasa
dishes.note: Smoked Carniolan pork sausage with garlic and pepper, served with mustard and horseradish.

dishes.name: Jota
dishes.note: A thick winter stew of beans, sauerkraut and potato, often with pork. Made for November.

dishes.name: Prekmurska gibanica
dishes.note: A layered cake of poppy seed, walnut, apple and cottage cheese.

places.name: Klobasarna
places.note: A small counter beside the cathedral that serves Carniolan sausage and little else. Quick, cheap and good.

places.name: Moji štruklji
places.note: A štruklji specialist with around a dozen fillings.

places.name: Gostilna na Gradu
places.note: Regional Slovenian dishes up at the castle, at higher prices. Book ahead.

history.name: Roman Emona
history.note: The Romans built the town of Emona here about two thousand years ago. Stretches of its wall still stand south of the centre.

history.name: The 1895 earthquake
history.note: A strong earthquake damaged much of the city. The rebuild brought the Art Nouveau facades you see around Prešeren Square.

history.name: Plečnik's city
history.note: Between the wars the architect Jože Plečnik reshaped Ljubljana: the Triple Bridge, the Central Market and the riverside embankments are his. UNESCO listed his work here in 2021.

history.name: A young capital
history.note: Slovenia declared independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, making Ljubljana a national capital.

nightlife.name: The riverside
nightlife.note: Bars and terraces line both banks of the Ljubljanica. Tozd, on Gallusovo nabrežje, is an easy first stop. In November, how lively it gets depends on the weather.

nightlife.name: Dvorni Bar
nightlife.note: A wine bar beside Congress Square with a long list of Slovenian wines.

nightlife.name: Nebotičnik
nightlife.note: The café and bar at the top of a 1933 skyscraper, with views to the castle. Best at sunset.

nightlife.name: Metelkova
nightlife.note: Clubs and live music in a former army barracks. Each space runs its own nights, so check what is on. It can feel empty when little is happening.
